```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Initial Setup - Folders and .gitignore
```{bash}

mkdir -p data/raw data/processed scripts genomics_work outputs/figures outputs/gee_maps docs

cat << 'EOF' > .gitignore
# RStudio session & history files
.Rhistory
.RData
.Rproj.user/

# Large bioinformatics & raw data files (prevents GitHub 100 MB push errors)
data/raw/*.fastq*
data/raw/*.fq*
genomics_work/
*.bam
*.bai
*.sam
*.fasta
*.fa
EOF
```

 Stream inly needed reads into RStudio
```{bash}
 
 # Stream 20,000 E. coli Nanopore reads (~100-150 MB)
fastq-dump -X 20000 --stdout SRR_ECOLI_ACCESSION > genomics_work/ecoli_sub.fastq

# Stream 40,000 marine seawater Nanopore reads (~200-300 MB)
fastq-dump -X 40000 --stdout SRR_SEAWATER_ACCESSION > genomics_work/seawater_sub.fastq

# Merge into a single simulated flood-plume seawater metagenome
cat genomics_work/ecoli_sub.fastq genomics_work/seawater_sub.fastq > genomics_work/plume_seawater.fastq
```

Assemble subsampled Oxford Nanopore seawater + E. coli reads in metagenome mode
```{bash}

flye --nano-hq subsampled.fastq \
     --meta \
     --out-dir flye_out \
     --threads 4

# Verify that assembly_graph.gfa was created
ls -lh flye_out/assembly_graph.gfa

```

```{bash}

# 1. Start Bandage metadata CSV
echo "Name,Color,Taxon" > flye_out/bandage_ecoli.csv

# 2. Extract contig names from your E. coli MetaBAT bin and assign Okabe-Ito orange
# Replace bin.1.fa with whichever bin matched ~50.8% GC and ~4.6-5.0 Mb
grep "^>" metabat_bins/bin.1.fa | sed 's/>//' | awk '{print $1",#D55E00,E_coli_MAG"}' >> flye_out/bandage_ecoli.csv

head flye_out/bandage_ecoli.csv
```
